Class MKCSlotInput

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.core.MKCSlotInput
@Internal public final class MKCSlotInput extends Object
Internal client-side input resolver for panel-hosted registered slots — the hover/click half of the panel-unified SlotElement path, and the slot-context enforcement of §0046 (a panel makes what it covers inert, in every context). Driven from MKCSlotScreenHook, which feeds it the active panel ids from SlotElementRegistry; not a consumer surface.

The gap this closes

Registered MKCSlots are appended last to menu.slots, so vanilla's getHoveredSlot — which returns the first hovering slot — resolves to the vanilla slot beneath a slot, not the slot itself. A revealed slot is then visually on top (its SlotElement renders it inline) but would be click-through: §0037's "everything behind a panel is inert" never reached it, because §0037's enforcement keys off MenuKit's panel registry and a registered slot's hover resolution is keyed off the slot, not the panel box. This helper supplies the slot-context resolution.

What it does

resolveHoveredSlot(AbstractContainerScreen, double, double) answers, for a screen point:
  • over a revealed registered slot → that slot wins (hover + click route to it over the covered vanilla slot);
  • inside a revealed registered panel but between slots → blocked (the covered vanilla slot is inert — §0046 / §0037 bounding-box);
  • elsewhere → pass (vanilla resolution proceeds untouched).
Hidden (inert) registered panels contribute nothing — they neither win nor block, matching their inertness (§0021).

How it is wired (library-owned)

MenuKit's AbstractContainerScreen mixins (getHoveredSlot / mouseClicked) fire the neutral SlotScreenHook dispatch, which MKC fulfils with MKCSlotScreenHook. That hook calls resolveHoveredSlot(AbstractContainerScreen, double, double) with the panel ids that currently host a SlotElement: the getHoveredSlot hook makes the registered slot win hover, tooltip and the click target (vanilla routes the click to whatever getHoveredSlot returns); the mouseClicked hook makes the panel's empty space inert so a click in a gap can't fall through and drop a carried item. No consumer mixin is involved.

Client-only

References client screen types; only ever loaded client-side. The slot itself (MKCSlots) carries no client types and runs on both sides.

    • resolveHoveredSlot

      public static MKCSlotInput.Resolution resolveHoveredSlot(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen, double mouseX, double mouseY, @Nullable Set<String> panelFilter)
      Resolves the slot under (mouseX, mouseY) considering only the revealed slots whose panel id is in panelFilter (or all slots when panelFilter is null). The screen dispatcher passes the active panels for the current screen so an opted-out slot neither wins hover nor blocks the slot behind it.

      Recognises slots directly and through the creative SlotWrapper (MKCSlotAccess.asMKCSlot). On a hit it returns the slot that is actually in menu.slots — the raw MKCSlot on the survival inventory, the SlotWrapper on the creative screen — because the caller (vanilla getHoveredSlot) routes the click to whatever this returns, and creative's click path requires the wrapper.

      Safe on any container screen — one with no matching revealed slots returns MKCSlotInput.Resolution.PASS.
